answer: A farm of quiet copies cannot outrun a cost that compounds with each alias. First influence opens only at dawn: one delayed, fully clawable deposit from a payer who has never funded this operator, signed at an hour no lock-step cluster can occupy together. Auditors then peel a public shale of work strata — timestamps, hosts, and signing kernels stacked in order — and slash any layer that matches another identity. What remains is a single pearl of attested receipts, slow to form and fully reversible if fusion is later proved, so minting extras is a net loss, not a shortcut.
